specification.problem: Estimate systematic amplitude and off-resonance errors of single-qubit gates with Heisenberg-scaling precision, robustly to SPAM errors, using only single-qubit experiments; the abstract names a robust version of Higgins et al. phase estimation as the key tool but gives no explicit formulas.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: a background single-qubit amplitude-error model (rotation angle pi(1+epsilon)) and repeated-gate Ramsey-style phase-estimation likelihood with depth-m sequences, in one tiny instance (m in {1,2,4,8}). The robust phase estimation theorem, off-resonance error estimation, SPAM-robust protocol details, and error bounds are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: fractional amplitude error of the nominally pi rotation
number of gate repetitions in an experiment
accumulated phase/rotation angle to estimate, theta = pi*epsilon
probability of measurement outcome 0 after m repetitions
number of shots per depth m

equations.label: Amplitude-error gate model
equations.description: Nominal pi rotation about X with fractional over/under-rotation epsilon.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions amplitude errors in single-qubit gates but gives no model; this is a standard parametrization chosen for the instance.
assumptions: Pure rotation about X with no other errors

equations.label: Repeated gate
equations.description: Applying the gate m times multiplies the rotation angle by m, amplifying epsilon linearly in m (the source of Heisenberg scaling).
equations.justification: Commuting powers of the same rotation; Heisenberg scaling in general arises from phase amplification by depth.
assumptions: Coherent error identical in every repetition

equations.label: Outcome probability
equations.description: Ideal-SPAM probability of measuring 0 starting from |0> in the Z basis.
equations.justification: Direct computation from eq_2. For m even, the dependence on epsilon is cos^2(m pi epsilon/2); for m odd it is sin^2(m pi epsilon/2).

equations.label: Empirical frequency
equations.description: Binomial estimate of p_m from N shots.

equations.label: Heisenberg-scaling target
equations.description: Error shrinking inversely with total gate applications, rather than as 1/sqrt of the count.
equations.abstract_quote: our estimates achieve the optimal efficiency, Heisenberg scaling
equations.justification: Abstract claims Heisenberg scaling; the specific form in terms of m_max is an inference, not a stated bound or constant.

registers.name: q
registers.role: single data qubit; no ancilla or entanglement

specification.initial_state: |0> (assumed ideal; the actual protocol is claimed robust to SPAM errors, details not given)

steps.description: Choose depths m in {1,2,4,8} and shot count N per depth.
Prepare |0>, apply the gate U(epsilon) m times.
Measure in the Z basis and compute the empirical frequencies.
Combine results across depths to refine the estimate of epsilon, coarse to fine, as in phase estimation; the robust combination rule is not given.

specification.measurement: Computational (Z) basis measurement of the single qubit after m gate applications.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Invert p_m for epsilon at increasing depths, using coarse estimates to resolve ambiguity at larger m. The robust Higgins-type procedure and its SPAM-robust analysis are not specified in the abstract.
assumptions: Amplitude-error model on an X rotation was chosen by me
Ideal SPAM used for the tiny instance
missing_information: Robust phase estimation theorem statement, depth schedule, and error bounds
Off-resonance error model and the universal gate-set sequences used
